name: broken-reference-call-returned-event-unknown-call
description: A `call_returned` event naming a pair no runnable of its component calls asynchronously (contract `12.7.0`, `rule:swc.call-returned-event.unknown-call`): the event is admissible on its own -- its `port` and `operation` are non-blank names and the member address is well formed -- and the assembled result names no asynchronous call point for it, so pass D refuses it as a `broken-reference` at the event's `operation`.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model. `ExampleConsumerSWC` requires `IExample` through `rIn` and calls nothing; the event below names `ReadDtc` of `rIn`, which no runnable of the component calls. The repair is the call with `asynchronous: true` on the runnable that makes it, in the same change set, or another pair; the refusal names no candidate, because the nearest declared name is not the call the event means.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the requested address exactly, so the refusal is pass D's and not the scope gate's.

input.intent: Start ExampleConsumerRun when the ReadDtc call through rIn returns.

expected.notes: The address is the referrer, the event's `operation`, not the call point that is missing: an event left behind when its call is removed is refused the same way. A pair two runnables call asynchronously is a `consistency-violation` instead (`swc.call-returned-event.ambiguous-call`). The model stays byte-identical.
